question: Under one fixed additive 29-residue running-key rule, does any contiguous offset of the archived Emerson text produce LP2 openings that score above matched full-search controls and carry into a held-out continuation?
source_rule: Join all 50 stored Emerson paragraph texts with one space, uppercase, retain ASCII A-Z only, map A=0 through Z=25; one source letter supplies one rune shift; no wrap.
cipher_rule: Plaintext rune index = ciphertext rune index minus source shift modulo 29. Keep source advancing at every alphabet rune, ignore punctuation. Start each target page at its first rune.
source_offsets: Every zero-based contiguous offset with at least 192 source letters remaining.
controls: Eight deterministic full-stream letter shuffles, seeds 330100–330107, searched with the identical offset and scoring procedure; one planted additive ciphertext from the first 192 decoded indices of LP1-06 at Emerson offset 3301.
score: Average English quadgram base-10 log likelihood of concatenated canonical GP Latin labels; unseen grams count 0.01, model in pinned file. Select highest score on first 96 decoded runes, tie break at lowest offset; evaluate next 96 only after selection.
decision: Report all full-search maxima and holdouts descriptively; no generic running-key exclusion or p-value from eight shuffles.
